title: Inhomogeneous Deformation Triviality Verification Artifacts for C(n+1)
summary_theorem: An inhomogeneous deformation gamma_gb of C(n+1) is trivial (i.e., gamma_gb = delta f for an odd map f) if and only if all deformation parameters gb_{sigma, j, s} vanish identically.

analytical_proof_outline.step_1: Evaluate gamma_gb(Z, F_{sigma, j, s}) where Z is the so(2) generator. Finds Z-component equal to sigma * gb_{sigma, j, s}.
analytical_proof_outline.step_2: Evaluate coboundary (delta f)(Z, F_{sigma, j, s}). Since [Z, sp(2n)] = 0 and {F, F} has no Z component, Z component of delta f is -sigma * c_{sigma, j, s}.
analytical_proof_outline.step_3: Equating Z components forces f(F_{sigma, j, s}) = -gb_{sigma, j, s} Z + sp(2n) terms.
analytical_proof_outline.step_4: Evaluate (delta f)(F_{sigma, j, s}, F_{sigma, k, t}) for odd generators. Coboundary term yields +sigma * gb_{sigma, j, s} F_{sigma, k, t}, whereas deformation term is -gb_{sigma, j, s} F_{sigma, k, t}.
analytical_proof_outline.step_5: Equating coefficients requires -gb_{sigma, j, s} = sigma * gb_{sigma, j, s}, forcing gb_{+, j, s} = 0.
analytical_proof_outline.step_6: Evaluating mixed odd-odd brackets forces gb_{-, j, s} = 0 for all j, s.
